newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Wallonia presents social plan for Clabecq.
newsitem.headline: Wallonia presents social plan for Clabecq.

text.p: Belgium's Walloon regional government, main shareholder of bankrupt steel firm Clabecq, on Monday put forward a social plan for the firm's 1,800 workers following talks with unions, receivers and federal ministers.

In a statement the cabinet of Walloon government president Robert Collignon said the proposal concerned among other things early retirement, the problem of workers over 50, and the allocation of money made on the sale of stock.

"This plan forms a whole package, and accepting it and putting it into practice must allow the conditions to be created for the company's activities to be taken over and for the social consequences of bankruptcy to be alleviated," it said.
Clabecq steel workers were expected to vote on the proposal on Thursday, Belgian radio said.

Since the firm was declared bankrupt in January its angry employees have staged numerous demonstrations, some violent, in Brussels and at the steel works itself near the town of Tubize about 30 km south of the Belgian capital.
Meanwhile Walloon region officials and Clabecq's court-appointed receivers have been trying to find a buyer for the company, which suffered from high costs, poor margins and low-quality products.
On Friday Italian-based private steel and commodities trading group Duferco was named as an interested candidate.

Clabecq's death sentence was signed in December 1996 when the European Commission rejected a regional aid plan, say it was inadmissible state aid for a firm without a future, and the Walloon region pulled the plug on further funding.
